brief: Blue Horizon, a fictional company, reported an unusual download from an internal shared drive. Investigate the entry point, affected account, event timeline, and recommended response. All domains and addresses are fictional training data.

evidence.title: E01 — Suspicious Email
evidence.text:
2026-11-18 08:42 AST
From: helpdesk@blue-horiz0n.example
To: nada@blue-horizon.example
Subject: Shared drive verification
Body: Please verify your account before 09:00.
Link: https://login.blue-horiz0n.example/verify
Official domain: blue-horizon.example

evidence.title: E02 — Authentication Log
evidence.text:
08:45 user=nada source=10.0.5.24 result=FAILED reason=bad_password
08:46 user=nada source=10.0.5.24 result=SUCCESS mfa=passed
08:51 user=nada source=198.51.100.42 result=SUCCESS mfa=not_required
08:53 user=salem source=10.0.5.19 result=SUCCESS mfa=passed
09:01 user=nada source=198.51.100.42 result=SUCCESS mfa=not_required

evidence.title: E03 — File Access Log
evidence.text:
08:47 nada 10.0.5.24 GET /shared/meeting-notes.pdf 200 88KB
08:55 nada 198.51.100.42 GET /shared/customer-list.csv 200 1.8MB
08:56 nada 198.51.100.42 GET /shared/customer-list.csv 200 1.8MB
08:58 salem 10.0.5.19 GET /shared/policy.pdf 200 40KB
09:02 nada 198.51.100.42 POST /shared/export 200 1.8MB

evidence.title: E04 — SOC Alert
evidence.text:
Alert ID: BH-2026-114
09:03 AST — Unusual sign-in followed by repeated access to customer-list.csv
IP 198.51.100.42 is TEST-NET documentation address in this exercise.
No endpoint malware alert recorded.
Incident status: Investigation pending

evidence.title: E05 — Employee Statement
evidence.text: Nada: I opened a message at 08:43 and entered my password into a verification form. I did not approve a second sign-in. I was working from office 10.0.5.24 all morning.

questions.text: What is the first clear sign of phishing?
options: The domain differs from the official domain
The email arrived in the morning

questions.text: Which account should be investigated first?
What is the first unexpected login from outside the internal network?
Which IP address is linked to the suspicious activity?
Which file may have been accessed without authorization?
Which evidence best links the suspicious login to file activity?
options: Matching account, IP address and timing

questions.text: What is the most appropriate first containment action after confirming the suspicion?
options: Revoke suspicious sessions and reset credentials

questions.text: What is the most accurate conclusion based on the available evidence?
options: Salem is proven to have stolen data
There is strong evidence of account compromise and unauthorized access; the export impact needs further verification

questions.text: Which evidence records the employee’s own account of the event?
What does the SOC alert explicitly say about malware?
options: No endpoint malware alert was recorded

questions.text: Which security principle is most directly at risk when customer records are accessed without permission?
Which statement distinguishes an observation from an inference?
options: The export proves all records were stolen
The logs show repeated access; the final impact still needs verification

questions.text: Which action helps prevent similar incidents?
options: Strengthen phishing awareness and authentication policies
